Subject: Correction: GST formula in my takings template

I need to correct an error in my free daily takings and GST template.

In versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2, column F worked out GST on inclusive takings by multiplying the total by 9%. That is wrong. For takings that already include GST, the GST portion is 9/109 of the total.

Ravi Subramaniam spotted the problem, and Shu Fen confirmed it. Thank you both for taking the time to check and raise it. In Ravi’s example, a day’s GST-inclusive takings of $1,090 produced GST of $98.10 in the old sheet. The correct amount is $90, a difference of $8.10.

I tested version 1.0 against my own sample figures, but those figures were already exclusive of GST. The check passed, and I missed the error in the inclusive calculation. That was my mistake. There is no excuse for it, and I understand why Melvin is upset: people trusted the template in part because I am an accountant.

The error affects versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2. There have been 412 downloads since 12 August. I corrected the formula and uploaded version 1.3 on 8 November.

The issue affects people who entered GST-inclusive takings in the old versions — which is how most hawkers record receipts. If your entries were all amounts excluding GST, this formula error did not affect your GST calculation. The quarterly Box 1 sales total was calculated independently and was correct in versions 1.0 to 1.2. It was Box 6, the output tax figure, that could be overstated.

In version 1.3, check that the setting in H2 matches the amounts you enter. Choose “prices exclude GST” only when your entries exclude GST. For receipts that include GST, use the inclusive setting — even if the prices on your menu exclude GST.

If you already filed your Jul–Sep F5 using the sheet, here is what to do:

1. Find out which version you used and check whether you entered GST-inclusive takings. If you used version 1.0, 1.1 or 1.2 with inclusive takings, check the Box 6 figure against the corrected calculation.
2. Keep a copy of your filed return and the records and sheet you used.
3. Contact IRAS or your filer before making any correction. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error should be corrected in a later F5 or through a GST F7. Please check the IRAS errors page and get advice from your filer on the right route for your situation.
4. If you have not filed yet, stop using the old version and download version 1.3.

The old formula overstated GST; it did not cause anyone to underpay IRAS. Some people may have overpaid, and should check the correction route with IRAS or their filer. I will update the template page if there is anything else users need to know.
